Can reproduce on HEAD. Looks like a NULL pointer deref (possibly in libvterm?)
Backtrace:

More minimal repro (still requires fzf):
```vim
split
lcd /
terminal fzf --reverse --height 80\%
call timer_start(1000, {-> execute('quit')})
```

The floating window doesn't seem to be necessary, but interestingly the creation of a new window (e.g: `split`) is required?

In `terminal_receive`, `term->vt->rows` is 5, which makes me think the ol' dummy window from `win_alloc_aucmd_win` is involved somehow (similar to the crashes in #14887). This is not the case for when `split` is omitted (the crash doesn't happen in that case). Maybe we need a `terminal_check_size` call somewhere?

Looks like this might be a duplicate of #13966, but this issue has a more general repro that doesn't require vim-floaterm.

---

Seems `refresh_timer_cb` calls `refresh_terminal` -> `aucmd_prepbuf` (`win_alloc_aucmd_win` creates a dummy window with 5 rows) -> `win_config_float` -> `terminal_check_size`, which sets `term->vt->rows` to 5. Skipping the resize for autocmd windows seems to fix the crash (should we even bother resizing for those?), but I'm not yet sure _why_ the resize crashes...

Hmm, just had a look at this again. I suspect this may indeed be a libvterm bug?

The cursor is at row 0 before the crash. The resize to 5 rows in `vterm_set_size` causes libvterm to call `resize`, which gives `delta->row = -5` [here](https://github.com/neovim/libvterm/blob/nvim/src/screen.c#L507), which is added to the cursor row position in `on_resize`, making it -5. This position causes `getcell` to return `NULL` inside of `erase_internal`. :thinking:
Awesome! The version bump indeed seems to fix the issue.

issue.title: segmentation fault when use `radian` in neovim's embedded terminal

labels.name: bug-crash
labels.description: issue reporting a crash or segfault

repository.name: neovim
repository.description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability

issue.body:
### Neovim version (nvim -v)

v0.7.0-dev+1294-g0c02e8a62

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

no 8.2.3489

### Operating system/version

macOS 12.2.1

### Terminal name/version

iterm2 3.4.15

### $TERM environment variable

xterm-256color

### Installation

homebrew build from source

### How to reproduce the issue

0. Have `radian` installed:[radian](https://github.com/randy3k/radian)

1. `nvim --clean` to start a minimal vanilla neovim.
2. `:set mouse=a` this is optinal to enable mouse support.
3. `:e xxx.txt` open any files.
4. `:sp` to vertical split the screen.
5. `<C-w> j` type control-w simulaneously and then release and type j, to move the cursor to the bottom split of the screen.
6. `:term` to open the terminal embedded in neovim.
7. `i` to enter the insert mode.
8. `radian` to enter the radian REPL.
9. `<C-\><C-n>` to exit the insert mode, and return to normal mode. 
10. `<C-w> 100-` to shorten the width of radian's window
11. `<C-w> 20 +` to widen the width of radian's window
12. repeat 9, 10. an error may be triggered: `99564 segmentation fault` and neovim crashes.

if step 2 is done, step 10-12 can be replaced by simple using mouse to drag the upper frame of the radian's window.

Basically the problem is: if the window of radian is too small, it has the possiblity to suddenly crashed the entire neovim.
I've tested with other REPLs, including vanilla R, ipython, julia, they are fine, and I can arbitrarily drag the window.

This is not only happens in iterm2, it also happens in vimR, the GUI. But what happens for vimR is it totally freezes, and not quit back to the shell prompt. And the stable version $0.6.1$ also has this issue.


### Expected behavior

I can arbitrarily drag the window, just like using other terminal tools.

### Actual behavior

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/45728125/160515356-2c13936b-0c89-4397-b308-65fc314cc90c.mov

no

### Terminal name/version

kitty 0.24.4

### $TERM environment variable

kitty

### Installation

AUR

### How to reproduce the issue

Install [toggleterm](https://github.com/akinsho/toggleterm.nvim/) plugin
Install [fzf](https://github.com/junegunn/fzf)
Open neovim
Open toggleterm
Type fzf
Press command to close toggleterm

### Expected behavior

I expect toggleterm to close and not crash neovim

### Actual behavior

![togggleterm_bug](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/64891486/161290295-05a31fc4-e69a-4a91-b248-9eacc8dbe409.gif)

My toggle command is ```<C-c>```.
As you can see, the first time I pressed ```<C-c>```, it successfully toggled the terminal off, but the second time, neovim crashed.

Here's my config:

```lua

if not status_ok then
	return
end

local opt = { noremap = true }

	float_opts = {
		border = "curved",
		winblend = 0,
		highlights = {
			border = "Normal",
			background = "Normal",
		},
	},
})

function _G.set_terminal_keymaps()
	vim.api.nvim_buf_set_keymap(0, "t", "<C-q>", [[<C-\><C-n>]], opt)
	-- vim.api.nvim_buf_set_keymap(0, "t", "<C-h>", [[<C-\><C-n><C-W>h]], opt)
	-- vim.api.nvim_buf_set_keymap(0, "t", "<C-j>", [[<C-\><C-n><C-W>j]], opt)
	-- vim.api.nvim_buf_set_keymap(0, "t", "<C-k>", [[<C-\><C-n><C-W>k]], opt)
	-- vim.api.nvim_buf_set_keymap(0, "t", "<C-l>", [[<C-\><C-n><C-W>l]], opt)
end

vim.cmd("autocmd! TermOpen term://* lua set_terminal_keymaps()")

local Terminal = require("toggleterm.terminal").Terminal
local lazygit = Terminal:new({ cmd = "lazygit", hidden = true })

function _LAZYGIT_TOGGLE()
	lazygit:toggle()
end

-- map("t", "<esc>", "<C-\\><C-N>", opts)
map("n", "<Leader>gg", ":lua _LAZYGIT_TOGGLE()<CR>", opt)
```

I tried changing my toggle command to ```<C-t>``` and the bug is still there.
I can't reproduce on normal terminal.

Reported to toggleterm owner [here](https://github.com/akinsho/toggleterm.nvim/issues/189).
Following his suggestion to report the bug.

body: It seems the minimal repro no longer reproduces the crash even in an older version of Nvim, probably because of a change in fzf. Since libvterm has been bumped to version 0.3, I guess this can be closed.
